translations.en: 11 – Mūsā b. Janjawayh, Abū ʿImrān, al-Urmanī. Weak. He has a book.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Mūsā b. Janjawayh as a weak narrator (daʿīf) known as al-Urmanī, likely indicating his Armenian origin or residence, which was a common descriptor in early biographical dictionaries. His classification as weak suggests his hadiths may be accepted but not relied upon for establishing legal rulings, reflecting the rigorous scrutiny applied to narrators in Shia hadith sciences. The mention of his authored book highlights his contribution to the transmission of knowledge despite his individual reliability status.
en.seo_question: Who is Mūsā b. Janjawayh and what is his status in hadith narration?

key_terms.مُوسَىٰ بْنُ زَنْجَوَيْهَ: Mūsā ibn Janjawayh, a specific narrator
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in ʿilm al-rijāl for a narrator whose reliability is questioned
key_terms.كِتَابٌ: Book, indicating the narrator authored a work
